chunks: From him, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Khālid, from ʿUbays ibn Hishām, from Thābit, from Ziyād ibn Abī Ghiyāth, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him saying: When the obligatory prayer is due, then begin with it, and it will not harm you to leave the supererogatory prayer that comes before it.

And what you have also previously cited from the reports, that the beginning of the time is more excellent, confirms these reports as well. So how do you reconcile between them? We say: as for what is contained in the reports we cited earlier, that salat (prayer) at the beginning of the time is more excellent, it is to be understood as referring to the time that comes after the time of the supererogatory prayer. For the nawafil are only permitted to be performed in advance until the passing of the measure of two feet or one cubit. Then when that has passed, it is not permissible to occupy oneself with the nawafil; rather, one should begin with the obligatory prayer. And that time is more excellent than the time after it, which is the time of the compelled person and those with excuses. We have already clarified earlier what indicates that, and have treated it fully in our larger book, and this further clarifies it.

key_terms.أَوَّلَ الْوَقْتِ: the beginning portion of the prayer time, regarded as more excellent
key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: the supererogatory prayer performed in addition to the obligation
key_terms.النَّوَافِلَ: optional devotional prayers performed before or around obligatory prayers
key_terms.الْأَعْذَارِ: legal excuses that justify delaying the prayer
key_terms.الْفَرْضِ: the obligatory duty, here the prescribed salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْمُضْطَرِّ: the one under compulsion who prays in a later, excused time

ai.seo_question: How are hadiths about praying at the earliest time reconciled with reports allowing supererogatory prayers before ẓuhr and ʿaṣr?
ai.summary: This passage explains the ruling on prioritizing the obligatory prayer once its proper time has arrived, even if this means leaving a recommended supererogatory prayer. It also reconciles reports about the excellence of praying at the earliest time by distinguishing between the limited window for nawafil and the superior time for beginning the obligatory salat (prayer).
